 Live Updates Updated Tue, Nov 10 2026 8:38 AM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email S&P 500 futures drop after higher-than-expected CPI reignites inflation concern: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Hugh Leask Lee Ying Shan Ananya Chetia Traders work on the floor of the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images S&P 500 futures fell on Tuesday as traders reacted to a pivotal consumer inflation report as well as new comments from a key Federal Reserve official.
 Futures tied to the broad market index traded down 0.5%, while those linked to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were around the flatline. Nasdaq-100 futures slipped 1.2%.
 Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech Tuesday that he thinks a December rate hike is likely. He also opened the door for a larger half-point increase next month as inflationary pressures persist. 
 "While the precise timing of the hikes doesn't matter, ensuring that the promised hikes are implemented in a reasonable period of time does," he said. 
 Waller's comments came ahead of the October consumer price index report , which came in hotter than expected. Headline CPI showed a 0.4% rise last month, above the gain of 0.3% that economists polled by Dow Jones expected. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, rose 0.3% in October. Economists had called for growth of 0.2%.
 Annual figures were not be provided for Tuesday's report because of the 2025 government shutdown. At that time, the Bureau of Labor Statistics was unable to collect some data which means there isn't a comparable figure for the index. 
 Across the Atlantic, the pan-European Stoxx 600 was 0.64% higher. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 added 0.26%, with France's CAC 40 rising 0.88% and Germany's DAX up 0.94%.
 In Asia, South Korea's Kospi surged 4.3%, while Japan's  Nikkei 225 added 2.89%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 0.42%, and mainland China's CSI 300 added 0.26%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 1.27%.
 During the regular U.S. trading day, the Dow Industrials gained 1,104 points, or 2.2%, while the S&P 500 popped about 2.4%. The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.7%. Monday's rally came after a rocky week for markets, in which traders grew concerned about the potential for a slowdown in data center buildouts after Democrats posted big victories in the midterm elections.
 3 Min Ago CPI rises more than expected in October
 The consumer price index rose by 0.4% month over month in October , reigniting inflation fears as traders brace for a potential Fed rate hike in December. Economists polled by Dow Jones expected an increase of 0.3%.
 — Fred Imbert 
 24 Min Ago Sanmina, Skydance and Casella Waste Systems among the stocks making moves before the bell
 Sanmina : Shares soared 19% after the electronic manufacturing services provider rolled out an outlook that came in ahead of the Street's expectations.
 Skydance : The stock fell more than 2% after the entertainment conglomerate formed from Paramount and Warner Bros.
 Casella Waste Systems : Shares fell more than 5% after its quarterly results fell short of expectations.
 Check out CNBC's live blog to read more about the stocks making premarket moves here .
 — Deena Zaidi 
 44 Min Ago What to expect from the upcoming report on where inflation stood in October
 A sign displays the price of regular gasoline and diesel fuel as drivers refuel vehicles at an Irving gas station in Sherman, Maine, US, on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. Graeme Sloan | Bloomberg | Getty Images Falling gasoline prices provided some relief to consumers in October, but Federal Reserve officials are increasingly concerned that inflation pressures elsewhere in the economy are proving harder to contain.
 Prices at the pump declined by more than 4%, according to the Energy Information Administration, providing a respite from a surge that had added more than a dollar a gallon over the past year.
 However, the consumer price index for the month, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics will release Tuesday at 8:30 a.m., is expected to show only a slight let-up.
 Read the full story here .
 — Jeff Cox 
 1 Hour Ago Anthropic sets price range of $70 to $78 in upcoming IPO
 Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, on screen, virtually attends a United Nations Security Council meeting during the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, US, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. John Lamparski | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares in its upcoming IPO at a price range between $70 to $78 per share, according to an updated filing on Tuesday, bringing the five-year-old artificial intelligence lab a step closer to a potentially historic Nasdaq debut.
 At the high end of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion in proceeds through the IPO. The company could end up being worth up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from the $965 billion valuation it announced as part of a funding round in May.
 Read more here .
 — Ashley Capoot 
 2 Hours Ago Fed's Waller says December rate hike is likely
 Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller speaks during The Clearing House Annual Conference in New York City, U.S. November 12, 2024. Brendan McDermid | Reuters The Federal Reserve needs to follow through on an expected rate hike next month to maintain credibility, said Governor Christopher Waller , who also suggested a larger half-point increase may be warranted. 
 He said he is "leaning toward" a December increase, adding he would support "more robust action" if inflation readings are higher than expected. 
 "In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said. "Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take."
 — Fred Imbert 
 4 Hours Ago Nvidia stock edges higher as pressure mounts following alleged China spy links
 Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Nvidia shares edged higher in premarket trading Tuesday as investors continued to weigh the potential fallout from CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
 Nvidia shares closed more than 4% lower on Monday, the day after Huang  told staff in an email  that he had been "unfaithful" to his wife and had "fallen short" of his responsibilities as CEO.
 Nvidia stock edges higher as investors weigh potential fallout of CEO's affair with alleged spy 5 Hours Ago European chip stocks rise
 Shares of European semiconductor firms rose in early trade, led by Infineon , which gained 4.8%. 
 The German semiconductor manufacturer posted a record fourth quarter on Tuesday, and forecast revenue growth of more than 20 percent in 2027. It said it expects revenue from power supplies for data centers to reach close to 4 billion euros ($4.5 billion) next year. 
 Analysts at Citi said in a note Tuesday morning that Infineon's data center power forecast "provides a positive signal on underlying AI and data center demand despite recent concerns around deployment timelines."
 Also notching gains on Tuesday were Dutch chipmaking equipment manufacturer ASMI , up 2.4%, and Be Semiconductor , which rose by 2.9%. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 5 Hours Ago European shares open higher
 Europe-listed stocks opened broadly higher on Tuesday, building on strong gains seen in the previous session. 
 The pan-European Stoxx 600 rose 0.9% shortly after the opening bell, with most sectors and all major regional bourses up. France's CAC 40 led gains, on a rise of 1.2%. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 6 Hours Ago Oil prices continue to fall as Trump says fresh Iran strikes ‘unlikely’
 Crude oil futures were lower on Tuesday, extending a sharp decline that began last week. 
 As of 2:25 a.m. ET, front-month Brent crude oil futures were 1.3% lower at $91.45 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures shed 1.3% to trade at $85.70 a barrel. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Crude oil futures U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters Monday that fresh U.S. strikes on Iran were "highly unlikely," adding that "Iran militarily is effectively over."
 Global benchmark Brent crude futures are currently down 6.9% for the week, after losing 16.4% the previous week on hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the Iran war. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 6 Hours Ago South Korea's Kospi jumps over 4% as Asia-Pacific markets rise
 Asia-Pacific markets closed in the green on Tuesday. 
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 closed 2.87% higher at 60,459.58, while the Topix was up 1.98% at 3,893.71.
 South Korea's Kospi jumped 4.39% to end the trading day at 5,239.13, while the small-cap tech-heavy Kosdaq Index advanced 4.48% to 667.61.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 1.1% to 9,129.
 China's CSI 300 inched marginally higher to 4,059.11, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng index climbed 0.38% in its last hour of trade.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 6 Hours Ago TSMC’s October sales jump as global chip boom rolls on
 Leading chip manufacturer Taiwan Semiconductor hosted a rare U.S. event, the Open Innovation Platform Ecosystem Forum, in Santa Clara, California on Sept. 23, 2026. Katie Tarasov | CNBC Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co . on Tuesday reported October revenue of 586.89 billion New Taiwan dollars ($17.88 billion), up 59.7% from a year earlier and up 14.7% from the previous month.
 The world's largest contract chipmaker benefited from strong demand for advanced semiconductors, as major technology companies continue to invest heavily in artificial intelligence.
 TSMC's October sales jump as global chip boom rolls on
 6 Hours Ago German chip maker Infineon posts double-digit annual revenue growth
 Matthias Balk | picture alliance | Getty Images German semiconductor maker Infineon posted an 11.5% year-on-year jump in annual revenue for its 2026 fiscal year, with revenues coming in at 16.35 billion euros ($18.36 billion) – in line with analyst estimates. 
 Operating profit reached 2.2 billion euros, up from 1.5 billion euros the previous year. 
 In guidance issued alongside its results on Tuesday morning, Infineon forecast full-year revenue of around 20 billion euros for 2027. 
 "Infineon closed the fiscal year 2026 with another record quarter and enters the new fiscal year with continued strong momentum," CEO Jochen Hanebeck said in a statement. "Supported by an ongoing cyclical recovery and strong demand in our structural growth areas, we expect a significant increase in revenue and profitability in fiscal year 2027. Our semiconductor solutions for data center power supplies, the expansion and modernization of energy infrastructure, electromobility, and software-defined vehicles will be key contributors."
 — Chloe Taylor 
 8 Hours Ago SoftBank Group shares surge 13% as Asian tech stocks track Wall Street rebound
 Asian technology stocks surged Tuesday, tracking a rebound on Wall Street overnight as a sharp decline in oil prices lifted sentiment while renewed buying in chip names spilled over into Asia, following last week's bruising sell-off.
 Japan's technology investment giant SoftBank Group surged 13.4%, while chip-testing equipment maker Advantest gained 2.36%. Semiconductor equipment maker Tokyo Electron rose over 4.73%, while Lasertec and Disco advanced 6.74% and 6.01%, respectively.
 South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 5.2%, while Samsung Electronics rose 3.9%. Samsung SDI climbed 6.87%. Taiwan's TSMC added 0.45%.
 China's tech-heavy ChiNext Price Index rose 1.4%.
 The gains followed a strong session on Wall Street, where the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite climbed 2.74%, while the S&P 500 rose 2.35% to clock its best day since April 8.
 The recovery came after a steep sell-off in global technology stocks last week, fueled by concerns that Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections could lead to tighter restrictions on data-center development, potentially impacting demand for artificial intelligence chips and infrastructure.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 10 Hours Ago China imports top estimates in October as surplus narrows — but crosses $1 trillion in 10 months
 SHENZHEN, CHINA - MAY 1: The Chinese national flag is seen in front of stacked shipping containers bearing MSC (Mediterranean Shipping Company), Maersk, and Hamburg Süd branding at Yantian Port on May 1, 2026, in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, China. Cheng Xin | Getty Images News | Getty Images China's exports and imports surged more than expected in October, according to official data released Tuesday, while its surplus shrank sharply, undershooting estimates.
 Goods exports soared by 35.2% last month from a year earlier, exceeding expectations for a 33.5% jump in a Reuters poll but slowing from the 36.3% growth in September.
 Imports climbed by 41.6% last month, customs data showed, jumping from 31% in September and sharply beating Reuters-polled analysts' estimates of a 32% rise.
 The trade surplus dropped to $105.3 billion in October, the lowest level since April, according to LSEG data, with year-to-date figure at $1.04 trillion, compared to a record $1.2 trillion for the full year 2025. Calls from trading partners have grown louder for Beijing to boost domestic demand and balance its economy.
 — Anniek Bao 
 Correction: This post has been updated to reflect that the data was released on Tuesday. 
 13 Hours Ago South Korea's stock exchange temporary halts buy-side trading on Kospi as index surges
 The Korea Exchange activated buy-side trading curbs on both benchmark Kospi on Tuesday as the index surged over 5%.
 The exchange triggered a "sidecar" mechanism, suspending program buying for five minutes. The mechanism is activated when the Kospi 200 futures index gains 5% or more for at least one minute.
 The Korean index, dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix, has been seeing heightened volatility as AI plays have come under increased investor scrutiny.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 13 Hours Ago South Korea's Kospi jumps 5% as Asia markets open higher
 Asia-Pacific markets opened higher on Tuesday, as investors bought the dip in tech stocks.
 South Korea's Kospi surged 5.09%, while the small-cap, tech-heavy Kosdaq Index popped over 4.73%.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 added 2.78%, while the Topix rose 1.77%. 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was up 1.19%.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 14 Hours Ago Chicago Fed's Goolsbee expresses concern on inflation ahead of CPI report
 Ahead of the consumer price index reading set to roll out Tuesday morning, Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee flagged inflation fears. 
 "We go around, we talk to people everywhere in this district, all we hear about is affordability on the business side, the cost,"  said he said at a Monday event in his home district. "So we've got to come to terms with this cost-side and inflation-side failure."
 Goolsbee added the build-out related to artificial intelligence is also heightening the concerns. 
 "Now this stuff with the AI data center build-out is, to my eyes, starting to look more just like old-fashioned demand overheating," he said.
 Read more from CNBC's Jeff Cox on what to expect in the CPI report out Tuesday here .
 — Ananya Chetia 
 14 Hours Ago Trump says Jensen Huang told him he didn't know his affair partner 'was a spy'
 NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and U.S. President Donald Trump shake hands at an 'Investing in America' event in Washington, D.C., U.S., April 30, 2025. Leah Millis | Reuters President Donald Trump said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang denied to him on Monday that he knew the woman he had an extramarital affair with "was a spy" for China. 
 "I asked him that question: 'Did you have any idea that she was a spy?' He said, 'I had no idea that she was a spy,'" Trump told reporters at the White House.
 The president's comments come after Huang admitted on Sunday that he had an extramarital affair . The Nvidia board then announced it would initiate an investigation following recent reporting that Huang had been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort." 
 The New York Times reported on Oct. 29 that Alice Huang, who had developed a close relationship with the Nvidia executive, had come under scrutiny by U.S. spy agencies and "American officials had concluded that she was a Chinese intelligence asset, funneling information to Beijing." 
 Read more from CNBC's Dan Mangan about Trump's comments on Jensen Huang here .
 — Ananya Chetia 
 14 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to track Wall Street rally as oil drops, tech rebounds
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to rise on Tuesday, tracking gains on Wall Street overnight as a sharp decline in oil prices and a rebound in technology stocks lifted investor sentiment.
 Futures for Japan's  Nikkei 225  in Chicago were at 61,035 while in Osaka they were last at 60,930, compared with the index's previous close of 58,775.5.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 24,506 compared with the index's last close of 24,448.73.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was up 0.79% in early trade.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 15 Hours Ago Stock futures were flat on Monday.
 Stock futures traded near the flatline on Monday. 
 S&P 500 futures gained just 0.07%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 12 points, or 0.02%. Nasdaq-100 futures were up 0.19%.
 — Ananya Chetia
